title: Discover installed capabilities and operations
summary: Read installed product overviews and list capabilities and operations so an agent can select plausible entries and read their complete operating contracts.
use_when: A request may map to an installed local capability or adaptive operation.
The exact supported outcome, effects, authority, recovery, privacy, or invocation must be understood without inspecting source code.
The caller wants an installed product overview or its complete feature and operation inventory.
The selected installed registry's structure or cross-provider documentation compatibility must be diagnosed.
do_not_use_when: The correct capability is already known and its current contract has already been read in this session.
The task is ordinary work with no plausible installed-system catalog need.
outcome: The caller receives a product overview and inventory, a complete or filtered catalog, or one complete installed contract. Discovery executes no represented action.
effects: Reads explicitly indexed JSON and Markdown from installed provider bundles.
Writes no provider state and performs no readiness probe.
CLI dispatch separately attempts a metadata-only command-usage append; recording errors preserve the catalog result.
authority: Provider bundles are authoritative for documented support and semantics.
Chancery is authoritative only for structural validation, installed catalog discovery, and presentation.
The represented product remains authoritative for runtime readiness and domain success.
success: List reports every structurally valid installed entry, including deprecated or dependency-unavailable entries, with visible registry issues.
Show returns the complete version-matched contract and manual for an installed entry.

Product returns the owning provider identity, release, scope when published, overview or explicit not_published status, and its complete entry inventory. Provider-filtered list selects that exact owner. Both retain registry issues.
No documented invocation is executed as a side effect of discovery.
Doctor returns complete selected-registry validity, provider and entry counts, and structural or documentation-compatibility issues without probing represented products.
failure_and_recovery: A malformed provider is excluded and reported without hiding structurally valid providers.
A missing or incompatible dependency makes the affected entry unavailable until the owning provider is installed or updated.
Use doctor to inspect registry structure; use the provider's own operating contract for live readiness.
An unknown or excluded product ID returns provider_not_found; a valid provider without an overview remains readable with overview_status not_published.
privacy: Installed documentation is processed locally and is not retained by Chancery.
Chancery has no network or model integration.

interfaces.label: Read a product overview and inventory

consumers.statement: Interactive agents and local readers that need an installed product overview, the catalog, or one exact product-owned contract may use this read-only capability.

preconditions.statement: The selected registry directory exists, and product installers have published any provider selectors the caller expects to discover.

inputs.statement: List accepts optional exact provider ID, mode, and kind filters; product accepts one exact provider ID; show accepts one exact stable entry ID. Doctor accepts the selected registry with no product-specific health inputs.
Natural-language request text is not an input to Chancery and is not matched or ranked by this capability.

outputs.statement: List returns IDs, titles, and summaries grouped by mode, with shared status defaults and entry exceptions. Product returns provider identity, schema, promise scope when published, indexed overview or explicit not_published status, and all owned entry cards. Both preserve registry issues. Show returns identity, provider release, dependency and readiness status, issues, and the complete manual once. --full adds structured authoring fields and normalized claims. JSON output schema 3 uses the same content selection. Doctor returns valid, registry, providers, counts, and issues; an invalid report retains its data with ok false and exit 1. Rust callers use the provider-owned chancery::api::Client and output types.

data_semantics.statement: The provider declares support. Availability means the installed bundle is structurally valid. Compatibility describes documentation dependencies. Discovery does not establish readiness.

identity_and_units.statement: Provider ID, provider release, stable entry ID, entry contract version, and provider schema version are distinct identities and versions.
Discovery publishes no domain measurement or quantitative unit.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Unfiltered list is complete for every explicitly indexed entry in every structurally valid provider fixed during that invocation. Product and provider-filtered list select the exact provider; additional list filters narrow its entries. Invalid providers and registry issues remain visible. The overview is the complete indexed Markdown text, or explicitly not_published; Chancery does not synthesize it.
Each invocation rereads the selected installed registry and retains no earlier catalog snapshot.
Starting represented capabilities or probing their runtime readiness is outside catalog discovery.

access.statement: Access is a local read of an absolute registry path or the current user's default Chancery registry; indexed inner symlinks and path escapes are rejected.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Each invocation canonicalizes every selector once and constructs one deterministic view in memory. It prints that view and exits without writing provider or registry state.
Malformed providers are excluded as units. Duplicate global entry IDs are excluded, regardless of filesystem order. Dependency unavailability propagates transitively.

operational_limits.statement: Bounds are 1,024 provider selectors, 4,096 indexed entries per provider, 1,048,576 bytes per manifest or entry, 4,194,304 bytes per manual or overview, and 65,536 UTF-8 bytes per text field. The bundle feature owns the full validation rules.
No wall-clock discovery latency or registry-size service-level objective is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: This reader accepts provider schemas 1, 2, 3, and 4. Only schema 4 permits the optional indexed overview. Earlier schemas remain readable with no overview. Removed schema-1 routing metadata is ignored only for schema 1, and unknown fields remain errors.
No retirement date is promised here for legacy provider schema support.

reliances.statement: Discovery creates no runtime, data, authority, or readiness reliance on a represented product; installed provider documentation is its local input.
